summary: Built a 3-node MariaDB Galera cluster (node1, node2, node3) from scratch on RHEL9 (installed mariadb:10.11/galera module, configured wsrep, opened firewalld ports 3306/4444/4567/4568, verified SELinux port labels), bootstrapped node1 and joined node2/node3 via rsync SST, created an application database (appdb.customers) with sample rows, and confirmed multi-master writes replicate across all three. Added node4 as a fourth Galera member: installed the same stack, configured wsrep with the existing cluster's seed list, started it, and confirmed it received the full dataset via SST and both reads and writes work symmetrically across all four nodes (wsrep_cluster_size=4, Synced). Then executed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured per-node boot_id and cluster health baselines, restarted each of the four nodes one at a time via `systemctl reboot` (never more than one down at once, preserving Galera quorum), polled until each came back, confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and verified MariaDB auto-started, rejoined the cluster (size 4, Synced, wsrep_ready ON), and retained all data (7 rows) after each restart. Finished with a live cross-node write/read check (node1 write visible instantly on node4) proving the cluster is fully healthy post-restart.
actions_performed: Installed mariadb:10.11/galera module (mariadb-server, mariadb-server-galera, galera) on node1-node4
Populated /etc/hosts on all nodes from CLUSTER_HOSTS
Opened firewalld ports 3306/4444/4567(tcp+udp)/4568 on all nodes and verified SELinux mysqld_port_t labels
Configured /etc/my.cnf.d/z-galera-custom.cnf with wsrep settings on node1-node3 (fixed a file-ordering bug where 99-*.cnf sorted before galera.cnf and got overridden)
Bootstrapped Galera on node1 via galera_new_cluster after wiping the mis-initialized datadir
Set MariaDB root password via generated on-node secret
Created appdb.customers table with 5 seed rows
Joined node2 and node3 to the cluster via systemctl start mariadb (rsync SST), verified wsrep_cluster_size and data sync
Verified multi-master replication with a write from node2 visible on node1/node3
Enabled mariadb service on boot for node1-node3
Configured node4 with wsrep_cluster_address including all four nodes and started it, confirming SST delivered full dataset and wsrep_cluster_size=4
Verified node4 accepts writes that replicate to node1-node3
Enabled mariadb on boot for node4; updated node1-node3 seed lists to include node4
Captured pre-restart boot_id and cluster-health baseline on all four nodes
Restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 sequentially (one at a time) via systemctl reboot, polling each until reachable again
Verified changed boot_id and full Galera recovery (cluster_size=4, Synced, wsrep_ready ON, 7 rows intact) after each node's restart
Performed a final cross-node write (node1) and read (node4) to confirm full cluster health after all four restarts

evidence.requirement: 3-node Galera cluster established on node1/node2/node3 holding application data
evidence.summary: node1 bootstrapped (wsrep_ready ON, cluster_size 1 then Primary), appdb.customers created with 5 rows, node2 and node3 joined via SST and both report cluster_size 2/3 with the same 5 rows present.

evidence.requirement: Cluster accepts writes from any of the original 3 members (multi-master)
evidence.summary: Insert executed on node2 is visible on node1 and node3 immediately afterward.

evidence.requirement: node4 added as a fourth member carrying existing data
evidence.summary: node4 configured with wsrep pointing at the existing cluster, started, and confirmed wsrep_cluster_size=4 with the full customers table (including the pre-existing Frank-from-node2 row) present via SST.

evidence.requirement: node4 accepts writes like the other members
evidence.summary: Insert executed on node4 (Grace-from-node4) is visible on node1, node2, and node3, all reporting wsrep_cluster_size=4.
